August 12, 2026

Passport by Molina Healthcare

Molina Healthcare, Inc.  
P.O. Box 36030  
Louisville, KY 40233-6030  

Re: Member: Reese Iverson  
Member ID: W871184265  
Plan: Passport Health Plan by Molina, Kentucky Commercial/ACA  
Reference number: POC-7908FD6832-14323  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. The denial states that the documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The submitted clinical records establish the diagnosis, severity, failed conservative treatment, functional impairment, and medical circumstances supporting the requested procedure:

- I have had nine months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 17, 2026, through June 23, 2026, including 16 visits for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening. Bracing was also used. These treatments are documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 25, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on July 13, 2026, showed a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci were intact, and there was no significant arthritis.
- I have recurrent instability with pivoting and have given way twice on stairs.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The requested surgery was recommended by Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.
- The records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

This information addresses the reason given for denial by supplying objective imaging, examination findings, documented functional instability, duration of symptoms, and extensive unsuccessful conservative treatment. It also addresses relevant factors affecting surgical risk and appropriateness.

I understand that Passport’s public materials state that it uses MCG guidelines and may use Molina Clinical Policies when applicable. However, the denial notice does not identify the specific guideline, edition, section, or documentation requirement applied to CPT 29888. I have not quoted the plan’s medical-necessity policy because Passport has not identified or provided that policy in the denial notice, and I have not retrieved a publicly available policy containing ACL-reconstruction criteria specific to this plan. Please identify the exact criteria applied and provide the applicable guideline or policy, including its edition and relevant section, if the denial is not overturned.

Please reverse the denial and approve ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, based on the complete ACL tear, recurrent instability, objective MRI and examination findings, failed conservative care, and the medical recommendation from orthopedic surgery. If additional information is required, please specify exactly what is missing and allow my treating provider an opportunity to submit it.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing. This appeal must be received no later than February 8, 2027.

Sincerely,

Reese Iverson  
Member ID: W871184265
